newsitem.title: UK: Arjo cuts costs, boosts profits.
newsitem.headline: Arjo cuts costs, boosts profits.

text.p: Cost-cutting combined with improvement in second-half trading conditions boosted pretax profits of Anglo-French paper and packaging group Arjo Wiggins-Appleton Plc.
The group, hit by declining pulp prices in the last two years, on Thursday reported pretax profits of 133.9 million pounds in 1996 compared to 72 million in the previous year.
The company's turnover rose marginally to 3.57 billion pounds from 3.56 billion and it maintained its dividend at 7.5 pence per share.

Recovery of trade conditions in the second half of the year offset weak volumes and pressure on margins which depressed its 1996 first half pretax profits to 32.3 million pounds from 135.3 million in the previous year.

Company officials at Arjo, which demerged from B.A.T Industries Plc in 1990, said they expected pulp prices to weaken slightly, around six percent, over the next six months, but it was not expected to affect the company's performance.
